# Request regarding baggage safety measures

2026.04.14

On the Tateyama Alpine Route, we ask that you take safety precautions for any luggage (skis, snowboards, backpacks, etc.) that may endanger other passengers or damage or soil other luggage when using public transport.If safety precautions are not in place, we ask that you purchase a simple cover (bag) on-site.

\[Requests Regarding Use of Tateyama Highland Buses\]

Large backpacks will be loaded into the trunk of the Tateyama Highland Bus.Please take precautions to prevent damage to valuables and leaks from water bottles, etc. Also, please remove fragile items such as helmets and cups from your backpack. Please note that we cannot accept any responsibility for damage resulting from failure to take safety precautions.

\[Requests Regarding the Handling of Mobile Batteries\]

When using mobile batteries in stations or on trains, please be extremely careful not to drop them or subject them to impact. Please refrain from using mobile batteries that are swollen or overheated due to deterioration, etc., in stations or on trains. In the event that you see any fire or smoke, please remain calm, ensure your safety, and immediately inform a staff member.

\[Request to passengers carrying bear spray\]

There have been incidents of bear spray being misfired due to improperly attached safety pins. If you are carrying bear spray, please cooperate with the following points while at the station or on public transport:① Please ensure that the safety pin on your bear spray is securely attached. ② Please seal your bear spray in a plastic bag. ③ Please place the sealed bear spray in your backpack.

# Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route – Your ultimate guide to the journey crossing the Japanese Alps

- [September 10, 2023](https://danae-explore.com/en/2023/09/10/)
- [Danae](https://danae-explore.com/en/author/danaedalbianco-com-br/)

![Ilustração da Rota Alpina Tateyama Kurobe, com meios de transporte e altitudes entre Toyama e Nagano, no Japão.](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan__-73.jpg)

**A journey across several modes of transport through some of Japan’s most dramatic landscapes, set among its highest mountains**. Come with me as I cross the Japanese Alps along the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route!

While flipping through the Lonely Planet guidebook, I found a short mention about this route crossing the northern Japanese Alps — where **different modes of transport take you through snowy peaks and breathtaking scenery, starting at 475 meters and reaching 2,450 meters, known as “the roof of Japan”**— I immediately knew I had to go.

**First of all, follow me on Instagram [@danae\_explore](https://www.instagram.com/danae_explore/) – that’s where you can keep up with my trips, find lots of travel tips, and send me a DM anytime. I love chatting about travel!**

The [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route](https://www.getyourguide.com/nagano-l5079/from-nagano-tateyama-kurobe-alpine-route-t237272/?partner_id=CPXHPCX&utm_medium=online_publisher&cmp=ratken&deeplink_id=2c2a53c2-ce53-58ec-8a8a-7b3a749bdfde&page_id=acdbeba5-b63e-5494-b698-2dbb0e22bac7) crosses a part of the **Chubu Sangaku National Park**, passing through Mount Tateyama, a.k.a. Mount Tate, which, together with Mt. Fuji and Mt. Hakusan, is **one of Japan’s three sacred mountains.**

_“In the 17th-19th centuries, Tateyama became one of Japan’s three holy mountains along with Mt. Fuji and Mt. Hakusan. Many pilgrims visited the mountain. People seeing hot water coming from the ground at Jigokudani imagined that they were seeing into the underworld. The high point of Mt. Tateyama overlooking the valley of hell came to represent heaven. People who climbed Mt. Tateyama during their life hoped that their souls would go to heaven after their death.”_ [https://www.alpen-route.com/en/info/history.html](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/info/history.html)

I didn’t find much information about the Alpen Route (as it’s also called) on the internet – what little I could find was on the [official route website](https://www.alpen-route.com/) and a few blogs. But even without knowing exactly what to expect, I decided to go for it and explore these landscapes.

It turned out to be an amazing experience, with stunning scenery that fit perfectly into [our 4-week Japan itinerary](https://danae-explore.com/en/japan-the-ultimate-4-week-itinerary/). It was a day when we stepped away from the traditional tourist attractions (big cities, temples, and shrines) and experienced a side of Japan that feels far from the one we usually imagine.

We loved Japan so much that we were back before long, this time in winter: [skiing in Sapporo](https://danae-explore.com/en/ski-itinerary-in-sapporo/), revisiting old favorites (hello again, [Tokyo](https://danae-explore.com/en/where-to-stay-in-tokyo/), [Hiroshima](https://danae-explore.com/en/2-day-itinerary-hiroshima-miyajima/) and [Kyoto](https://danae-explore.com/en/what-to-do-in-kyoto-in-4-or-5-days/)), and adding some new ones like Kanazawa and Himeji, and some of [day-trips from Tokyo](https://danae-explore.com/en/best-day-trips-from-tokyo/) we haven’t done before. Check it all out here on the blog or over on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/danae_explore/).

![Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, view from Daikanbo, Japan](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan__-62.jpg)

.

In this post, you will find:

[Toggle](https://danae-explore.com/en/tateyama-kurobe-alpine-route/#)

## Where is the Tateyame Kurobe Alpine Route

**The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route connects Nagano Prefecture (to the east) with Toyama Prefecture (to the west), in central-western Honshu (Japan’s main island)**.

The route is approximately 90 kilometers long, with an elevation difference of 1,975 meters.

You can travel the route from east to west (from Nagano to Toyama) or from west to east (from Toyama to Nagano). Most people travel it one way, but it’s also possible to go halfway and return the same way.

.

This is just the beginning, [Japan](https://danae-explore.com/en/asia-en/japan/) has so much more to offer. Here on the blog, alongside our full [4-week itinerary](https://danae-explore.com/en/japan-the-ultimate-4-week-itinerary/) from the first trip, you’ll find [accommodation tips for Tokyo](https://danae-explore.com/en/where-to-stay-in-tokyo/) and the best [day-trips from Tokyo](https://danae-explore.com/en/best-day-trips-from-tokyo/), complete guides for [Kyoto](https://danae-explore.com/en/what-to-do-in-kyoto-in-4-or-5-days/), [Hiroshima](https://danae-explore.com/en/2-day-itinerary-hiroshima-miyajima/), [Sapporo](https://danae-explore.com/en/ski-itinerary-in-sapporo/) and the charming post towns of [Magome and Tsumago](https://danae-explore.com/en/nakasendo-road-magome-tsumago/) for those looking to get off the beaten path.

![Kurobe Dam on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, Japanese Alps, Japan](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan__-21.jpg)![Mountains and vegetation around Kurobe Dam on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, Japanese Alps, Japan](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan__-59.jpg)

.

## Best time to visit the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route

The **[Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route](https://www.getyourguide.com/nagano-l5079/from-nagano-tateyama-kurobe-alpine-route-t237272/?partner_id=CPXHPCX&utm_medium=online_publisher&cmp=ratken&deeplink_id=2c2a53c2-ce53-58ec-8a8a-7b3a749bdfde&page_id=acdbeba5-b63e-5494-b698-2dbb0e22bac7)** operates from spring to late autumn, but the specific opening and closing dates vary from year to year. In 2024, it was open from April 15 to November 30. Check the [official website](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/) for the opening dates for each year.

The best time to visit the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route depends on the kind of experience you’re looking for, as each season has its own highlights.

**In spring, the main attraction is the snow corridor along the highest section of the route, between Murodo and Midagahara**. This road is lined with snow walls that can reach up to 20 meters high! Alongside the cherry blossoms, visiting this snow corridor is one of the best things to do in Japan during springtime. While the snow gradually melts, there’s usually still snow along the sides of the road until the end of June, depending on the year. We visited in mid-July, and as expected, the snow corridor had already completely melted.

.

**Summer is the best time to enjoy the hiking trails.** There are several options for all levels, including the one to the summit of Mount Tate (3,015 m above sea level).

**Autumn is marked by beautiful foliage, and it’s also possible to hike most of the trails.**

We did the Alpen Route on July 16 (peak of the Japanese summer), during our [month-long Japan trip](https://danae-explore.com/en/japan-the-ultimate-4-week-itinerary/). If you visit Japan in summer, be prepared for very hot weather.

We found the route to be quite crowded; almost everyone was a Japanese tourist, which we were told may have been due to July 17 being a national holiday that year (Ocean Day – Umi no Hi, celebrated on the third Monday of July).

We loved Japan so much that we were back before long, this time in winter: [skiing in Sapporo](https://danae-explore.com/en/ski-itinerary-in-sapporo/), revisiting old favorites (hello again, [Tokyo](https://danae-explore.com/en/where-to-stay-in-tokyo/), [Hiroshima](https://danae-explore.com/en/2-day-itinerary-hiroshima-miyajima/) and [Kyoto](https://danae-explore.com/en/what-to-do-in-kyoto-in-4-or-5-days/)), and adding some new ones like Kanazawa and Himeji. Check it all out here on the blog or over on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/danae_explore/).

.

## Where to stay on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route

The main accommodations options along the route are:

– [**Hotel Tateyama**](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/tateyama.en.html?aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken) **:** the only one still available when we were planning, but it was beyond our budget. **It is located at Murodo Station, the highest point of the Alpine Route, and the stay includes a walk through the snow corridor and stargazing activities**. As it is right at the station, it can get quite busy during the day.

– [**Midagahara Hotel**](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/midagahara.en.html?aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken): located at the station of the same name, **at 1.930 meters above sea level**. It tends to be slightly more affordable than the previous one and is also highly rated. Since it is not one of the main stations on the route, it tends to be quieter than Hotel Tateyama.

– [**Tateyama Kogen Hotel**](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/tateyama-kogen.xb.html?aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken): located at **Tengudaira Station**, at **2.300 altitude**, it looks like an excellent option in a quieter area than Tateyama.

– [**Tengudaira Mountain Lodge**](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/tengudairasansou-tian-gou-ping-shan-zhuang.en.html?aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken): also at **Tengudaira Station** one of the highest points along the route, with easy access to several hiking trails.

If you plan to do the route in a single day, as we did, it is best to stay in [Toyama](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.en.html?city=-246605&aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken) or [Shinano-Omachi](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.en.html?city=-240482&aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken). You can also stay in [Nagano](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.en.html?city=-237683&aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken), but that adds about 25 minutes to the journey.

## Baggage forwarding service at Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route

I had read online that **you’re not allowed to bring luggage on the Alpine Route**, but I saw several people with suitcases and wondered: if you’re staying at one of the hotels along the route, wouldn’t you need to bring your luggage?

In any case, even if it were possible, we chose to follow the rules and not bring any luggage — although we are experts at [traveling with carry-on only](https://danae-explore.com/en/how-to-travel-with-only-a-carry-on/), **carrying all those bags throughout the journey would turn it into a nightmare**, right?

Between Shinano-Omachi and Toyama, there is a baggage forwarding service available. You drop your bags off between 7:40 am and 10:30 am — in Shinano-Omachi, it’s right in front of the train station (practically next to the [hotel where we stayed](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/route-inn-shinano-omachi-ekimae-omachi.pt-br.html?aid=7942444&sid=48cbc27f7007224e9a4bbf06ec24a246&checkin=2023-09-14;checkout=2023-09-15;dest_id=-240482;dest_type=city;dist=0;group_adults=2;group_children=0;hapos=1;hpos=1;no_rooms=1;req_adults=2;req_children=0;room1=A%2CA;sb_price_type=total;soh=1;sr_order=popularity;srepoch=1694267764;srpvid=8d1161f5b60c0134;type=total;ucfs=1&#no_availability_msg&label=ratken)), and in Toyama, it’s close to the station’s ticket gates — and pick them up between 3:00 pm and 6:00 pm at the other end of the route. It costs ¥2,500 per item. The service doesn’t send luggage to Nagano, so if you’re staying there, you’ll need to take your bags to Shinano-Omachi and drop them off (or pick them up) there. The [official website](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/) has more details about this service.

## How to do the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route

**The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route can be done from east to west or the other way around, and there’s no right or wrong way.** It depends on what fits best into your itinerary. **You can also go as far as Murodo (the highest point) and return the same way**. We did the Alpine Route on our own, as I explain here, but it’s also possible to do it with an [organized tour](https://www.getyourguide.com/nagano-l5079/from-nagano-tateyama-kurobe-alpine-route-t237272/?partner_id=CPXHPCX&utm_medium=online_publisher&cmp=ratken&deeplink_id=2c2a53c2-ce53-58ec-8a8a-7b3a749bdfde&page_id=acdbeba5-b63e-5494-b698-2dbb0e22bac7).

**We did the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route it in a single day: we started in Shinano-Omachi by bus at 8 am and arrived in Toyama at 5:30 pm.**

.

![Illustration of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, with means of transport and altitudes between Toyama and Nagano, Japan.](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan_-5.jpg)

.

**This chart shows the different modes of transport, the travel time for each, and the transfer points.** But please note that in practice, each leg takes longer than it seems because of waiting and queue times.

In Shinano-Omachi, we took the bus in front of the train station and simply showed the QR code generated when purchasing the ticket online. The official Alpen Route website lists the bus schedules — just note that the departure time shown on your ticket refers to Ogizawa onwards.

**Upon arriving in Ogizawa, there is a large station with a shop and restaurant.** There, we exchanged our online ticket for a physical one at a kiosk, which we used for the entire journey. We then got in line and took the electric bus, which covers 6.1 km inside a tunnel and drops you off at Kurobe Dam. This tunnel was built to support the construction of the dam and is still used for its operation today.

.

![Kurobe Dam - Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, Japanese Alps, Japan](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan-32.jpg)Kurobem Dam, 1.470 meters above sea level

.

**Kurobe Dam sits at 1,470 meters above sea level.** It is nearly 500 meters long and 186 meters high, making it the tallest dam in Japan. During Japan’s post-war economic boom, the dam was built to help meet the country’s growing energy demand. Ten million people worked on its construction in the 1950s, and it represented a major engineering challenge, completed at the cost of 171 lives.

From there, you walk across the dam (about 800 meters) to reach **Kurobeko**, where you take the funicular (cable car) to the next stop.

**This funicular runs entirely inside a tunnel, covering about 800 meters**, with a vertical gain of 373 meters. At the end, **you reach Kurobedaira, at 1,828 meters above sea level**.

At this stop, there’s a viewpoint, a shop, and a restaurant, but we didn’t spend much time there. We got straight in line for the **aerial tramway, which takes you over 1.7 km to Daikanbo, at 2,316 meters**(the first photo in this post!).

From there, you take a trolleybus (through a tunnel) to **Murodo, the highest point on the route, at 2,450 meters above sea level.**

.

![Murodo - Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, Japanese Alps, Japan](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan-42.jpg)

.

**Murodo is, literally and figuratively, the highlight of the trip. It’s where you can see (and even climb) Mount Tate and where you’ll find some of the best hikes in the area.** There are also geysers, lakes, and a wide range of landscapes. We had quite a cloudy day, so the view of Mount Tate will have to wait for another time, but it was still beautiful!

Be prepared for much lower temperatures than at the beginning of the route. On the day we went, the difference was around 20°C (from 32°C in Toyama to 12°C in Murodo).

There are a few hotels in this area, such as [Hotel Tateyama](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/tateyama.en.html?aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken) (mentioned above), as well as campgrounds, shops, restaurants, and cafés.

One of the trails leads to Hell Valley, an area where strong sulfur-smelling vapors rise from a total of 136 vents in the ground. There is a walkway through the area, but it was closed due to safety concerns when we visited.

**From Murodo, a bus takes you to the famous snow corridor in spring**. When we went, on July 16, the snow along the road had already completely melted.

.

![Mount Tate - Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route - Japan - girl in pink hoodie, with her back to the camera, walking through the fog.](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan__-25.jpg)Murodo![Hell Valley, one of the main attractions at Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ](https://danae-explore.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Japan__-29.jpg)Hell Valley

.

If you want to stop at **Tengudaira Station or Midagahara**, take the bus that stops there. Otherwise, the bus goes directly to **Bijodaira (at 977 meters above sea level)**, with a photo stop (without getting off the bus) at **Shomyo Falls, the tallest waterfall in Japan**.

From Bijodaira, you continue on the **funicular (cable car) to Tateyama, at 475 meters above sea level.**

A local train (Toyama Chiho Railroad) takes you from Tateyama to Toyama, arriving at the city’s central station, with easy access to the JR station if you still have energy to keep going 😉 In Tateyama, you can also take an express train to Toyama (paid separately), which I would have taken if I had known about it when planning the trip.

We stayed overnight in Toyama at **[Toyama Chitetsu Hotel](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/toyama-chitetsu.en.html?aid=7942444&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2&label=ratken)**.

## How much does the Alpine Rout Cost (and how to buy tickets)

**The Alpine Route is not covered by the JR Pass.**

Tickets can be purchased directly on the [official Alpen Route website](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html). You’ll need to create a profile and follow the instructions, choosing the direction of your trip and your travel date. In the next step, you select the section you want to travel, the departure time from Ogizawa, and the number of people. The bus between Ogizawa and Shinano-Omachi/Nagano must be purchased separately, as the main route ticket starts from Ogizawa.

It’s also possible to purchase the route only up to Tateyama, from where you can take the express train to Toyama or continue to other destinations in Japan.

In 2023, the cost per adult for the Ogizawa–Toyama section was ¥12,360 (approx. US$77), or ¥10,940 (approx. US$69) for the Ogizawa–Tateyama section. The bus between Ogizawa and Nagano costs around ¥4.300, and between Ogizawa and Shinano-Omachi, ¥2.000 (prices updated in April/2026).

After purchasing, you’ll receive a ticket with a QR code, which you can exchange for a physical ticket in Ogizawa (or in Toyama/Tateyama).

[On this page](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html), you’ll find more information about tickets.

But if you prefer, you can do the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route with [tours like this one](https://www.getyourguide.com/nagano-l5079/from-nagano-tateyama-kurobe-alpine-route-t237272/?partner_id=CPXHPCX&utm_medium=online_publisher&cmp=ratken&deeplink_id=2c2a53c2-ce53-58ec-8a8a-7b3a749bdfde&page_id=acdbeba5-b63e-5494-b698-2dbb0e22bac7).

web.markdown:
# FAQ

## Transport

### QWhere is the starting point of the Alpine Route?

A

Tateyama Station (Toyama Prefecture, west side) and Ogizawa (Nagano Prefecture, east side).

### QWhat time are the first and last departures?

A

It varies depending on the season. Please see the [timetable](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/timetable/).

### QDo I need a reservation to ride?

A

Only the Tateyama Cable Car departing Tateyama Station, and the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus departing Ogizawa, require a designated boarding time. You can reserve a departure time when purchasing web tickets, but for other advance tickets and same-day tickets, boarding times must be reserved at the station’s ticket window. Reservations are not required at other stations, so please check the timetable and head to the boarding gate accordingly.

### QCan I get on and off the Tateyama Highland Bus along its route?

A

You can get off at Midagahara and Tengudaira. However, because all passengers are required to be seated, reservations are required to re-board the bus.

If you get off at Midagahara, please make your re-boarding reservation at Midagahara Station.

If you get off at Tengudaira, please make your reservation at Tengudaira Mountain Lodge.

### QCan I get off at each station for sightseeing?

A

You can enjoy sightseeing and walking around at each station during your transfers. Please check the timetable and ensure that you do not miss your transfer.

### QAre parking lots available if I come by car?

A

There are [parking lots](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/parking/) at Tateyama Station (Toyama side) and at Ogizawa (Nagano side). Cars are not permitted on the Alpine Route (between Tateyama Station & Ogizawa), so if you are passing through, please use the car [forwarding service](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/getting-here/#VehicleTransferService).

## Tickets

### QWhere can I buy tickets?

A

1\. Purchase your web ticket in advance through the [official website](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html). (You must collect your ticket from the ticket machine before boarding.)

2\. Purchase tickets in advance through a travel agency. Tickets must be exchanged, and departure times reserved, on the day of travel.

3\. Purchase [same-day tickets](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/same-day-tickets/) at Alpine Route stations. (Tickets cannot be purchased the day before travel.)

### QCan I purchase same-day tickets even if web tickets are sold out?

A

Yes. Even when web tickets are sold out, same day tickets will remain available, but your desired departure time may be fully booked and additional waits may be required.

### QWhat time does the ticket sales counter open?

A

At Tateyama Station it opens 20 min before the first departure time, and at Ogizawa Station it is 40 min in advance.

The Alpine Route ticket window at Dentetsu Toyama Station usually opens at 7:30 but may open as early as 5:00 on certain days. If you are departing Dentetsu Toyama Station early in the morning, please purchase only your train ticket at first, and then purchase tickets for the additional routes on your journey upon arrival at Tateyama Station.

### QCan I purchase or exchange tickets at the station ticket window on the day before travel?

A

Ticket purchases and exchanges cannot be made the day before travel. Please come to the ticket window on the day that you will use the tickets.

### QCan I pay by credit card?

A

Cards can be used at Dentetsu Toyama, Tateyama, Bijodaira, Midagahara, Murodo, Daikanbo, Kurobedaira, Kurobeko, Kurobe Dam, and Ogizawa stations.

### QDo I need to buy a ticket for each section of the route?

A

Both one-way and round-trip tickets are available and cover all sections to your destination. However, depending on the station, tickets for some sections may not be available.

### QI am staying at a hotel on the Alpine Route. Can I use my ticket the next day?

A

Your ticket is valid for 5 days from the first day of use, for both one-way & round-trip travel.

## Sightseeing

### QHow long does it take to see the sights along the Alpine Route?

A

The journey from Tateyama Station to Ogizawa usually takes 6-8 hours, including transfers and sightseeing time. It is expected to be particularly busy during the snow wall season and on Japanese holidays, so please allow yourself plenty of time.

See suggested [model course](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/how-to-enjoy/sightseeing/from-toyama/) for details."

### QWhen does the sightseeing water release take place at Kurobe Dam?

A

Water sprays continuously throughout the day from June 26 to October 15. The water release may be canceled due to weather conditions.

### QCan I fly unmanned aerial vehicles (drones)?

A

The use of drones is not permitted.

### QHow do I get to Mikurigaike pond?

A

Go up the stairs at Murodo Station and turn left from the rooftop. You will reach the photo spot in about 15 min.

### QHow do I get to the snow wall?

A

After getting off the bus at Murodo Station, the highest point of the snow wall is a 15 min walk from the designated entrance. Snow wall touring can be enjoyed from mid-April till late June.

### QWhen can I see the fall leaves?

A

The elevation changes by 2,000 m across the Alpine Route, so the best viewing time varies from spot to spot. Mid-September till early November is considered the best viewing time.

### QAre there any locations where I can enjoy hiking?

A

There are a variety of hiking trails in Murodo, as well as some in Midagahara and Bijodaira.

### QWhat are the temperatures and recommended clothing for each season?

A

### QWhat are the best places to stay, on and around the Alpine Route?

A

Toyama City, around Tateyama Station, Matsumoto City, Omachi City, Omachi Onsenkyo(Omachi Hot Springs) and Nagano City are good places to stay before or after visiting.

On the Alpine Route itself, accommodation is available at Midagahara Hotel, Mikurigaike Onsen (hot springs), Murodo Mountain Lodge, and Tengudaira Mountain Lodge.

## Facilities

### QIs there a baggage forwarding service?

A

A baggage forwarding service is available that allows you to collect your luggage on the same day. [See details here](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/baggage/).

### QIs there a car forwarding service?

A

There is a car forwarding service between Tateyama Station & Ogizawa. [See details here](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/getting-here/#VehicleTransferService).

### QAre there any coin lockers?

A

Coin lockers are available at Tateyama, Bijodaira, Midagahara, Murodo, Kurobe Dam, and Ogizawa stations.

### QAre there any locations where drinking water is available?

A

Water is available at Tateyama, Murodo, Kurobedaira, and Kurobe Dam stations. Please ask staff for more information at each location.

### QAre there any elevators?

A

Elevators are only in operation at Ogizawa Station and Tateyama Nature Conservation Center (Murodo). Please speak to a member of staff if you require assistance.

### QAre wheelchairs available?

A

Wheelchairs are placed at each station for backup and emergency use. However, it is not possible to use one chair continuously across the Alpine Route.

### QAre baby carriages available to rent?

A

We do not provide baby carriage rentals. Furthermore, we recommend using compact carriages as there are many stairs and transfers.

### QIs smoking permitted?

A

Smoking is permitted only within the designated smoking area at each station.

### QWill I be able to use my mobile phone and Wi-fi?

A

Mobile phones get reception at most stations.

Wi-fi is available, free of charge, at Tateyama, Bijodaira, Murodo, Daikanbo, Kurobedaira, and Kurobeko stations. E-mail authentication is required, so it’s convenient to register in advance.

### QAre there any ATMs?

A

There are no ATMs along the length of the Alpine Route.

# Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route – Roof of Japan

![Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route](https://i0.wp.com/www.wannabeeverywhere.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/DSC_0934b-Pano.jpg?fit=1500%2C477&ssl=1)

- January 3, 2022

**The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route** (立山黒部アルペンルート) is a spectacular route through the Northern Japan Alps. It became viral after the internet got flooded with pictures of immense 20-meter tall snow wall creating a Snow Corridor, which you can visit from April to June. But that is not the only sight you can be mesmerized with. The Japanese Alps offer bewitching views of mountain peaks, lush forests, pristine lakes, and sulfur-covered valleys all year round.

Completed in 1971, this route is commonly referred to as the “Roof of Japan”, traversing through Japan’s highest mountain range – the Hida Mountains. To cross the mountains, you would need to use various means of transportation, including cable cars, trolley-buses, coaches, and a ropeway. From **mid-April to November 30,** the route connects Toyama City in Toyama Prefecture with Omachi Town in Nagano Prefecture. Thanks to heavy snowfall, the passage is not accessible during the winter months. The Alpine Route is **only accessible by public transport** to preserve the surrounding nature and keep tourism attendance under control.

The Alpine Route is about **37 kilometers** long, and at its highest point, the route reaches Murodo Station, which at 2450 meters above sea level. From there, you can hike to Mt. Oyama (3,003 m), which is one of the summits of Mt. Tateyama (3015m) – one of Japan’s three sacred mountains – along with Mt Fuji and Mt Haku.

![https://www.alpen-route.com/en/transport/fare.html](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20753%20479'%3E%3C/svg%3E)https://www.alpen-route.com/en/transport/fare.html

We visited Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route during the beginning of November, being slightly too late to catch autumn leaves in the upper parts of the route. Nonetheless, we loved each part of it, being entirely hypnotized by stunning views.

## How much time does it take?

I would reserve the whole day to traverse the route and enjoy the sights along the way – the entire route of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine trip requires at least 6 hours. We left Omachi early in the morning to get ahead of the crowds and reached Tateyama Station when the sun was setting. While crossing, we took a boat trip on Lake Kurobe and did a little hike when we arrived at Murodo. Throughout the journey, we slowly enjoyed the scenery and took a lot of breaks for pictures.

However, if I were to plan it again, I would probably split the route into two days to enjoy more hikes up in the mountains. We fell in love with the scenery and felt like there was so much more to see and do there than what the time allowed us 🙂

## What to see

### Kurobe Dam

Kurobe Dam being Japan’s tallest dam (186 m high), is definitely a sight to behold. This challenging engineering project was finished in 1963 and claimed the lives of 171 people! It was also our first stop on our Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route.

It is especially worth visiting between late June and mid-October when the water is released from its spillway for spectators. The water is discharged at a rate of over 10 -15 tons per second! Even during the off-season, the grand dam is a sight to behold.

The views were incredible, with sparkling emerald green waters of Lake Kurobe on one side and the valley covered with autumn foliage on the other. When visiting the dam, make sure to walk down the stairs to Rainbow Terrace, from which you might chance upon seeing a rainbow created by droplets of water falling from the dam.

### Kurobedaira

Kurobedaira is the transfer station between the Tateyama Ropeway and Kurobe Cablecar.

Interestingly, 1.7 kilometers long Tateyama ropeway operates without any support towers between the lower and upper stations, making it Japan’s longest one-span ropeway.

### Daikanbo

**Daikanbo** is a transfer station between the Tateyama Ropeway and Tateyama Trolley Bus. We took there a very short break, snapped a couple of pictures from the terrace, and continued towards Murodo.

[![Daikanbo](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%201196%20798'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.wannabeeverywhere.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/DSC_0762b.jpg?ssl=1)

### Murodo

Murodo is a volcanic plateau culminating at 2,450m above sea level and the highest place of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Road. It’s the place where you can find the awe-inspiring “Yuki-no-otani” snow wall that can reach a height of up to 20m.

![https://www.westjr.co.jp/global/en/ticket/hokuriku-arch-pass/Explore_Japan/spot/toyama/tateyama-kurobe-alpine-route/index.html](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20653%20653'%3E%3C/svg%3E)https://www.westjr.co.jp/global/en/ticket/hokuriku-arch-pass/Explore\_Japan/spot/toyama/tateyama-kurobe-alpine-route/index.html

Murodo is the entry point for many hikes, both for experienced hikers and just occasional walkers. We visited in early November, and we were lucky enough that there was no snow yet covering the trails. As we didn’t have much time, we only managed to take a 2.4 km hike in the area while enjoying the vibrant autumn colors and breathtaking mountains. The most impressive was the view towards **Murodo’s Jigokudani** (Hell’s Valley), with sulfur clouds covering the sky. There used to be a pathway through the valley itself; however, it was closed down due to too large quantity of volcanic gases.

### Midagahara Wetlands

Midagahara is one of Japan’s most extensive alpine wetlands, lying on a highland plateau 1930 meters above sea level. Many hiking trails spread through the marshland, with many pathways following along elevated, wooden boardwalks.

It was one of the places I regretted I didn’t have time to enjoy. I saw a lot of pictures from it, and I was mesmerized by flower-covered marshland in summer and yellow, red flora during the autumn season.

**Tateyama Togen Highland Bus** runs between Murodo and Bijodaira Station. Pay attention though, not all of them stop at Midagahara Wetlands.

Shomyo Falls is one of the **tallest waterfalls in Japan**. Depending on the season, one to three waterfalls can be seen that fall from more than **350 meters high**. A dedicated bus line from Tateyama station takes tourists closer to the fall; however, it is not included in the Alpine Route ticket.

**Bijodaira** is the best place for Tateyama cedar viewing or bird watching. Take a stroll through the lush primeval forest and be amazed by the 1000-year-old cedar and large beech trees. There are a couple of hiking trails that look pretty interesting.

## When to visit

Regardless of when you decide to visit this mountain range, you will fall in love with incredible views. Each season offers different experiences, and I would definitely visit again when I am back in Japan.

### Spring

During spring, Murodo and Midagahara are still covered in snow, allowing you to experience the snow corridor with a 20-meter tall wall along which you can walk. A section of the snow corridor around Murodo is open to pedestrians, usually from mid-April to late June.

If you are lucky, you might see Raicho (Ptarmigan), birds that were once revered as messengers from God, now designated as a Special National Treasure, roaming around.

### Summer

Around June through August, mountains are covered with lush vegetation and alpine flowers, making it the perfect scenery for a fantastic hike. Kurobe Dam fills with meltwater, and tourists can see the impressive sight of water released from the dam.

### Fall

One of the most mesmerizing times to see the Japanese Alps is the fall when the trees turn red and yellow. The fall colors typically reach their best around Murodo and Daikanbo from late September to early October, gradually descending the mountain slopes and arriving at the lower elevations from late October to early November.

![https://www.alpen-route.com/en/seasonal-attraction/autumn.html](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%201098%20313'%3E%3C/svg%3E)https://www.alpen-route.com/en/seasonal-attraction/autumn.html

Follow this link for a detailed guide, how to pick the perfect time for _[autumn foliage](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/seasonal-attraction/autumn.html)_.

### Winter

Snow starts falling in November, and depending on the weather conditions and the amount of snow, it might not be possible to go through the whole route. You can always reach Murodo from Omachi’s direction as only Bijodaira – Murodo bus line might be suspended. However, be prepared that you might not be able to cross over mountains to Toyama.

After November 30, the route closes down for the winter, reopening again in April.

![https://www.alpen-route.com/en/seasonal-attraction/winter.html](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20982%20389'%3E%3C/svg%3E)https://www.alpen-route.com/en/seasonal-attraction/winter.html

## Tickets

An excellent guide about what ticket to choose is _[available here.](https://centrip-japan.com/article/1152.html)_

There are a couple of options available:

- **Tateyama Kurobe Option Ticket –** is a discount ticket available for 9800 yen exclusively to foreign tourists. The ticket allows for a one-way trip along the Alpine Route between Nagano and Toyama and can be bought at selected JR ticket offices. The ticket has to be purchased at least one day in advance. We chose this one as we already had JR Pass to travel around and we just wanted to cross the Alpine road once.

- **Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass** is valid for five days, allowing you to check both the Alpine route and the area.
- **Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Ticket** – valid for eight days, allowing you to check both the Alpine route and the area

## Baggage Forwarding Service

Delivery services are required as **no big baggage is permitted** along Alpine Route. Most of the hotels in the area offer baggage forwarding service, meaning you can just drop off your bag either in the hotel or train station and pick it back when you reach the destination. You need to request staff for the special tag, fill in your details and pay.

We were glad we didn’t have to drag our backpacks up the mountains, and we could just enjoy hiking without carrying 20 kg of extra weight.
